# LeanBCH.Opt CORE ⟂ TARGET manifest

The library is split along a **durable seam** between a reusable, value-generic
(`α`-opaque) stack-VM proof **CORE** and a concrete BCH-2026 **TARGET**. The split
is realized as an *umbrella-import* seam (not a physical directory reorg): every
proof module keeps its current path/name, and two umbrellas classify them.

## CORE — `LeanBCH.Opt.Core`

Reusable across any stack VM. Carries no byte-level wire encoding and no
structured-control opcode semantics.

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Basic` | abstract stack-VM model: `run`/denote, `StepOk` (see coupling note) |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Peephole` | local rewrite calculus (curated hand-written folds) |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.FoldTable` | complete generated fold table (2114 thms; window-complete over the stack-shuffle algebra; GENERATED by `tools/foldgen`, do not hand-edit) |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Passthrough` | passthrough rewrites |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Dag` | dependency DAG |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Scheduler` | DAG scheduler |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Simulation` | simulation refinement |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.StepLemmas` | step-level lemmas |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Compose` | `schedule_refines` |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.MoveArrange` | `schedule_refines_move_cond` |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.NoNullHome` | no-null-home invariant |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Floor` | floor lemmas |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.MovementFloor` | movement floor |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.NlcsFloor` | `movement_lower_bound_nlcs` |

## TARGET — `LeanBCH.Opt.Targets.CashVM`

BCH-2026-specific. These are the clean **leaves** of the module DAG (only
`Control` imports `Decompile`; no Core module imports either), so they sever
cleanly.

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Decompile` | byte-level wire encoding (opcode↔byte `0x76..`, parse, `<n> OP_PICK` folding) + decompile bridge theorem |
| `LeanBCH.Opt.Control` | structured control (IF/NOTIF/ELSE/ENDIF/BEGIN/UNTIL/VERIFY) with libauth BCH-2026 branch semantics (incl. the OP_NOTIF-on-falsy fidelity fix) + `whole_program_end_to_end` |

External to the Lean library: the `conformance/` runner (streams the official
`vmb_test` corpus through the VM; `Runner.lean` → the `vmbconf` exe) and its
build-time op-cost differential vs libauth (`conformance/cost/`).

## Residual coupling (deliberately in Core)

`Basic`'s concrete `Op` inductive + `step` semantics is BCH-shaped, but it is the
shared, value-opaque VM **model** that every module transitively needs (`Basic`
is the DAG root). Extracting it into the target would require parameterizing
`step` over the op set — a deep typeclass refactor touching all downstream
modules and every constructor-pattern-matching proof (high break-risk). It
therefore stays in Core, documented as the single Core-resident target coupling
that a downstream BCH port would re-model.

## Downstream porting recipe

`import LeanBCH.Opt.Core`, re-model the `Op`/`step` VM for your target, then supply
your own encoding + control analogues of `Decompile`/`Control`.
